transcript.text: panasonic nn h98 not heating anymore, any fix?

The simple possibilities are that it is set to defrost/low power, grill or combination rather than microwave heating. 1. Check the display/mode: select normal microwave cooking, not grill, combi or defrost, set full power, and use a microwave-safe cup of water.
2. Run it for one minute. Check whether the water is hot and whether the timer, light and turntable operate normally. This separates a settings issue from a heating-circuit or door-interlock fault.
3. Make sure the door closes firmly and the latch area is free of crumbs or damage. Do not force it. With a microwave-safe cup of water, does a one-minute cook on full microwave power leave it completely cold, and does the oven otherwise run normally (light/timer/turntable)?
water stays cold, stops after about 10-15 seconds with h98. fan, turntable and clock all work. grill heats fine. the model on the back is NN-CD87KSBPQ, h98 is just what the screen says

H98, no microwave heat, and a repeatable stop after 10–15 seconds point to the microwave high-voltage inverter/power circuit—not an overheating problem. The leading suspect is the inverter board; the magnetron is the next possibility and needs testing alongside it. The working grill, fan and turntable do not rule this out, as they are separate functions. There is no safe DIY internal fix for this. Do not remove the casing or try to test components: a microwave can retain lethal high voltage even unplugged. Avoid further microwave-heating tests and arrange a microwave engineer/Panasonic service assessment, quoting model NN-CD87KSBPQ and error H98. They should diagnose the inverter board and magnetron/feedback circuit before any parts are fitted. Whether it is worth repairing depends on the engineer’s quote, particularly if both the inverter and magnetron are implicated; if it is only the inverter module, repair can still be reasonable.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
